title: LangChain Raises $300 Million at $3 Billion Valuation Led by CapitalG
excerpt: LangChain's Series C brings total funding to $460 million, the company said. More than 7,000 organizations use LangSmith, its platform to run, improve and govern AI agents.
body:
• LangChain said it raised $300 million in a Series C at a $3 billion valuation, led by existing investor CapitalG, in its own announcement on November 13.
  • The round brings total funding to date to $460 million, Business Wire reported, with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth and existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures.
  • More than 7,000 organizations already rely on LangSmith, the company said, from startups such as Harvey and Rippling to enterprises including Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce.
  • LangChain said it will share several new LangSmith capabilities at a release event on November 20, 2026.

LangChain has raised $300 million in new funding at a $3 billion valuation, the company announced, in a Series C led by existing investor CapitalG. The round brings total funding to date to $460 million, according to the company's announcement carried by Business Wire.

Those are funding figures reported by the company itself, not earnings results. LangChain's announcement gave no revenue or profit figures, and no guidance — the numbers readers should take from it are the size of the round, the valuation the company stated, and the adoption figure it cited for its platform.

Who invested

CapitalG led the round, LangChain said in its own Series C announcement. New investors GIC and DFJ Growth participated significantly, alongside existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures. The round also included new investors Salesforce Ventures, Insight Venture Partners, QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures, and existing investors Sequoia, Amplify and Benchmark, the company said.

“Agents are going to transform how companies operate and the products they deliver. The companies that control these systems will build lasting competitive advantages.”

— Harrison Chase, Co-Founder and CEO of LangChain, in the company announcement

What the money is for: LangSmith

LangChain positions LangSmith as a framework-agnostic platform to run, improve and govern agents. More than 7,000 organizations already rely on LangSmith, the company said, from fast-growing startups like Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs to Fortune 500 enterprises like Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce. Clay uses LangSmith to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs per month, and Workday uses it to run and govern agents, reducing the time to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day, according to the company.

The company organises LangSmith around three pillars. Agent Runtime covers the architecture and infrastructure to run agents reliably, including Deep Agents, LangGraph and LangChain. Agent Improvement covers observability, evaluation and tools to test and improve performance. Agent Governance covers centralised control over how agents use models, tools and data, including model budgets and protection of sensitive data.

Mo Jomaa, a partner at CapitalG, said in the announcement: “The transition from experimental LLM applications to production-grade agents is one of the most significant shifts happening in enterprise software today.” CapitalG said LangChain had earned the trust of thousands of developers and global enterprises.

What to watch next

LangChain said it will share several new LangSmith capabilities at a special release event on November 20, 2026. That event is the next dated test of what the new capital is building. For developers and technology teams in the diaspora who build on LangChain's open-source frameworks, the commercial question the round raises is whether LangSmith — not the free frameworks — becomes the layer enterprises pay for to run agents in production. The company's stated answer, in its own words, is to enable every company to “own its intelligence”: choose models, control data and infrastructure, and govern agents at scale.
nri_angle: LangChain's agent platform is widely used by Indian-origin developers and enterprise teams building AI products, and its $3 billion valuation marks the scale of the agent-infrastructure market they work in.
